newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia approves unit trust joint venture firms.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia approves unit trust joint venture firms.

text.p: The Malaysian Securities Commission (SC) said on Monday that the government would allow 10 joint-venture foreign fund management companies to manage domestic unit trust funds.
In a statement, the SC said the ventures, which need at least 30 percent local equity, must meet criteria including managing at least $100 million in funds sourced from outside Malaysia.
The SC did not say which 10 firms it had identified, and a spokesman said he did not have a list of firms.
The firms "will have to show evidence of compliance with all necessary requirements before approval to manage any of the domestic unit trust funds is given", the statement said.

Malaysia has allowed foreign fund management companies with at least 30 percent local equity to manage local institutional funds since last year. But this is the first time that its approval has been extended to unit trust funds.
The SC said it opened up the unit trust fund sector because of "growing acceptance by retail investors of unit trusts as an efficient savings instrument".

The market regulator said the number of approved unit trust funds had risen from 39 in 1992 to 74 by September 30, 1996, with total net asset value of the funds growing from 15.7 billion ringgit to 56.1 billion during that period.
The ventures would tap outside expertise "in circumstances where in-house fund management capabilities cannot be properly developed", the SC said.
Of the 30 unit trust management companies in Malaysia, 10 have appointed external investment managers to manage some of their funds, the SC said.
